rule: rust-async-background-work: "missing timeouts" / "Does every long-running loop have a defined exit?" (checklist #22); the daemon must not hold a request open indefinitely.
summary: `quiesce_repo` cancels only cancellable jobs but then unconditionally awaits *every* active job with no timeout, so a `DeleteRepo` request blocks forever behind a non-cancellable job while holding the repository-deletion tombstone that rejects all other work for that repo.
failure_scenario: A user creates a worktree whose `postCreate` hook runs a long install (`pnpm install`, a container build). While that non-cancellable `PostCreateHooks` job runs, the user deletes the repository. `begin_repo_deletion` inserts the repo into `deleting_repos`, then `quiesce_repo` skips the cancel (`job.cancellable == false`) and parks on `wait(&job.id)`. The `DeleteRepo` request never completes — it occupies a slot in the connection's bounded `pending` set (server/connection.rs:140,153) and the app shows a hung dialog with no error — while `ensure_repo_available` (manager.rs:640-648) rejects every other operation on that repo with `Conflict("repository … is being deleted")` for the whole duration.
proposed_fix: Give `quiesce_repo` a bounded wait: `tokio::time::timeout(QUIESCE_TIMEOUT, self.wait(&job.id))` per job (or one deadline across the set), and on expiry return `DaemonError::Conflict` naming the job that could not be quiesced so `delete_repo_cascade` drops the tombstone (`RepoDeletionGuard::drop`, manager.rs:808-812) and reports an actionable error. Name the constant next to `cancellation_grace`/`cleanup_grace`.
test_plan: Add `#[tokio::test] async fn quiesce_reports_a_job_it_cannot_stop()` in `crates/fleet-daemon/src/jobs/manager/tests.rs`: `submit_for_repo(repo.clone(), JobKind::PostCreateHooks, "acme/api#x", "hooks", JobPolicy::new(false, false), |_| async { std::future::pending::<DaemonResult<()>>().await })`, then assert `matches!(manager.quiesce_repo(&repo).await, Err(DaemonError::Conflict(_)))` inside a `tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(2), …)` that must not elapse. Today the outer timeout elapses because `quiesce_repo` never returns.
verify_reason: Verified. jobs/manager.rs:670-678 cancels only `job.cancellable` jobs and then awaits every active job through `wait` (manager.rs:589-612), which loops on `updates.recv().await` with no deadline. Non-cancellable, arbitrarily long repo-scoped jobs genuinely exist: services/worktrees/post_create.rs:42 submits `JobKind::PostCreateHooks` with `JobPolicy::new(false, true)` (JobPolicy::new(cancellable, retryable) — manager.rs:76-81, so cancellable=false), and that job's future ends in `finish_detached_post_create`, which polls `while pid_is_alive(pid) { sleep(50ms) }` (post_create.rs:113-116) for the entire lifetime of the user's hooks. post_create.rs:210 and worktrees/trash.rs:144 are likewise `JobPolicy::new(false, false)`. The caller holds the exclusive tombstone across the wait: dispatch.rs:690-691 `let _deleting = self.jobs.begin_repo_deletion(&repo)?; self.jobs.quiesce_repo(&repo).await?;`, and `ensure_repo_available` (manager.rs:640-648) then rejects every other operation on that repo with Conflict. One correction to the failure narrative: the client does not hang forever — `request_timeout` (fleet-client/src/connection.rs:590-607) exempts only the CreateWorktree*/board requests, so `DeleteRepo` gets the 10 s `REQUEST_TIMEOUT` and the app surfaces a transport timeout. The real damage is daemon-side: the tombstone and the blocked repo outlive the request the user gave up on, with no way to clear them.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/jobs/manager.rs (quiesce_repo + a named timeout constant beside cancellation_grace/cleanup_grace), crates/fleet-daemon/src/jobs/manager/tests.rs, and the error surface of dispatch.rs `delete_repo_cascade` (a new Conflict variant reaching the app's delete-repo dialog copy). Check any e2e/integration test that deletes a repo while hooks are pending.
corrected_fix: Bound the wait, but do not let the deletion proceed on expiry — a `PostCreateHooks` job is still executing user commands inside the worktree, so timing out and deleting would race a live process. `tokio::time::timeout(QUIESCE_TIMEOUT, self.wait(&job.id))` per job, and on expiry return `DaemonError::Conflict` naming the job kind and target, so `delete_repo_cascade`'s `?` drops `_deleting` (RepoDeletionGuard::drop, manager.rs:808-812), the repo becomes usable again, and the user gets an actionable 'cannot delete: hooks for <target> are still running' instead of a transport timeout. Pick the timeout well under the client's 10 s REQUEST_TIMEOUT (connection.rs:35) so the error reaches the app rather than being replaced by a timeout, and log the non-quiesced job at warn.

rule: rust-async-background-work rule 10: "Fence blocking work at an ownership boundary" — no `std::fs::*` on a runtime thread, and never `.lock()` held over IO.
summary: `record_progress` and `append_log_line` perform `create_dir_all`, `OpenOptions::open` and buffered `writeln!` file IO while holding `JobManagerInner::state`, the one `std::sync::Mutex` that every other job operation (`list`, `record`, `cancel`, `submit`, `finish`, `prune`) also takes — all on tokio runtime threads.
failure_scenario: `fleet clone` runs `git clone --progress`, which emits a progress line every few milliseconds. Each line takes the global `state` mutex and issues a blocking write on the tokio worker thread that is draining the child's stdout. Concurrently, a connected app polling `ListJobs` calls `JobManager::list()` (manager.rs:453-455) which calls `prune` and then takes the same mutex — so client job listings, `cancel`, and every new `submit` (including `submit_boxed`'s own `append_log_line`, manager.rs:377) block behind whatever filesystem write the clone happens to be doing. On a busy or networked home directory the whole job registry stalls for the duration of a single `write`/`flush` syscall, and a runtime worker thread is blocked with it.
proposed_fix: Split the two concerns: under the `state` lock only mutate `job.record.progress` and take the `BufWriter` handle out (or a clone of the target path); release the guard; then write. Better, move log writing off the registry entirely — give each job an `mpsc::Sender<String>` drained by a single `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` writer task per job (or one shared writer task keyed by job id), so `record_progress` becomes a lock-free non-blocking send and the manager mutex is never held across a syscall.
test_plan: Introduce a `LogSink` seam on `JobManagerInner` (default: the current file writer) and add `#[tokio::test] async fn a_stalled_job_log_does_not_block_the_registry()` in `jobs/manager/tests.rs`: install a sink whose `write` blocks on an `mpsc::Receiver` (the `BlockingFiles` pattern from services/pool.rs:726-756), call `record_progress` from a spawned task, wait until the sink reports it is blocked, then assert `tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_millis(100), spawn_blocking(move || manager.list())).await.is_ok()`. Today the `list()` call blocks on the held mutex and the timeout elapses.
verify_reason: The structural claim is true but the evidence overstates the cost, and no stall is demonstrated. Real: jobs/manager/logs.rs:23-32 takes `lock(&self.inner.state)` (a std::sync::Mutex — the same one `list`/`cancel`/`submit`/`finish`/`prune` take) and calls `write_log` while holding it; `flush_log` (logs.rs:61-69) also flushes under it; and the callers are on tokio runtime threads (jobs/job.rs:98-107 passes the callback to `RealShell::run_streaming`, adapters/shell.rs:232+, whose line readers are ordinary tokio tasks). Overstated: `create_dir_all` and `OpenOptions::open` run once per job, not per line — logs.rs:37-49 memoises the writer in `job.log` (`slot @ None => ... slot.insert(BufWriter::new(file))`). So the steady-state per-line cost under the lock is a memcpy into an 8 KiB buffer, with a real `write(2)` only on each buffer boundary (roughly one syscall per 8 KiB of git progress). That is a genuine violation of the 'never hold a lock over IO' rule and a genuine tail-latency hazard on a networked home directory, but the claim that 'the whole job registry stalls' and that a runtime worker is blocked per progress line is not supported by the code, and I could not prove a measurable stall from reading alone.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/jobs/manager/logs.rs, the `log: Option<BufWriter<File>>` field on ManagedJob and its Drop/flush ordering in jobs/manager.rs, `tail` (logs.rs:7-15, which flushes before reading and must keep that ordering guarantee), jobs/job.rs callbacks, and jobs/manager/tests.rs (any test asserting log contents immediately after progress).
corrected_fix: Prefer the smaller change over the per-job writer task. Move the writer out of the `state`-locked `ManagedJob` into an `Arc<Mutex<BufWriter<File>>>` (or the log path) that `record_progress` clones out under the state guard; drop the state guard; then write under the per-job writer lock. That keeps line ordering per job — which a lock-free `mpsc` fan-out plus a shared writer task does not guarantee across the progress broadcast and `append_log_line` (manager.rs:377) — and keeps `tail`'s flush-then-read invariant intact, while removing all file IO from under the global registry mutex. If the mpsc/writer-task design is chosen anyway, `tail` must first await a flush barrier on that task or it will read a truncated log.

rule: rust-async-background-work: "Fence blocking work at an ownership boundary" + docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:91-93 ("Revision-keyed caches … let unchanged inventories be reused instead of rebuilt per request")
summary: Every dispatched request — including every terminal keystroke, mouse and wheel event — re-reads and re-parses `config.json` from disk behind one global async mutex, because `dispatch_routed_with_owner` starts with an uncached `config.load().await`.
evidence: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/dispatch.rs:31 `let config = self.config.load().await?;` — the first statement of the one function every request passes through. `ConfigStore::load` (crates/fleet-daemon/src/stores/config.rs:43-54) has no cache: `let guard = Arc::clone(&self.gate).lock_owned().await; … tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || { let _guard = guard; load_sync(&home, &path, files.as_ref()) })`, and `load_sync` (config.rs:114-131) does `files.exists(path)` + `serde_json::from_str(&files.read_text(path)?)` + `merge_config(home, patch)` every call, with `RealFiles::read_text` = `fs::read_to_string` (adapters/files.rs:264-266).
failure_scenario: A client attaches a terminal and types. `TerminalKey` is classified as a serialized terminal request (server/connection.rs:179 `body if terminal_request_is_serialized(&body)`) and reaches `run_terminal_request` → `services.dispatch_routed_with_owner` (connection.rs:462-464). So a 10-keystroke-per-second typist produces 10 `stat` + `read_to_string` + `serde_json` parses + full `merge_config` deep-merges per second, each one first taking `ConfigStore::gate`, a single process-wide `tokio::sync::Mutex`. Two attached terminals plus a `TerminalMouse`-reporting TUI serialize behind that one gate, so PTY input latency becomes a function of config-file IO — and a slow/contended disk turns typing into a queue.
proposed_fix: Cache the parsed `Config` in `ConfigStore` behind the existing `gate` (an `ArcSwap`/`Mutex<Option<Arc<Config>>>` invalidated by `save`/`update`, or a mtime+len check), and return `Arc<Config>` from `load()`. Alternatively, hoist the preamble out of the hot path: skip the `config.load()`/`machines.rebuild()`/`start_event_pumps()` prelude for request bodies that `terminal_request_is_serialized` classifies, since none of them consult `config`.
test_plan: Add `#[tokio::test] async fn dispatch_does_not_reread_config_for_every_request()` in `crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/dispatch.rs`'s test module: wrap `RealFiles` in a `CountingFiles` decorator (same shape as `BlockingFiles` in services/pool.rs:726-793) that increments an `AtomicUsize` whenever `read_text` is called on a path ending in `config.json`; build `Services` with it; run `services.dispatch(RequestBody::DaemonPing).await` 50 times; `assert!(reads.load(Ordering::Relaxed) <= 1)`. Today the counter reads 50.
verify_reason: The mechanism is exactly as described. crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/dispatch.rs:31 is the first statement of `dispatch_routed_with_owner`, and every request reaches it: connection.rs:179 classifies `TerminalKey`/`TerminalInput`/`TerminalMouse`/`WheelTerminal` as serialized terminal requests (connection.rs:479-495 `pty_input_request_is_ordered`) and connection.rs:462-464 calls `dispatch_routed_with_owner` for them. `ConfigStore::load` (stores/config.rs:43-54) has no cache at all: it takes `Arc::clone(&self.gate).lock_owned().await` — one process-wide tokio mutex shared with `save`/`update` — and then `load_sync` (config.rs:114-131) does `files.exists` + `serde_json::from_str(&files.read_text(path)?)` + `merge_config` on every call, with `RealFiles::read_text` = `fs::read_to_string` (adapters/files.rs:264-266). No config cache or watcher exists anywhere in the daemon (grep for notify/watcher over crates/fleet-daemon finds only session/child notifications). Two corrections to the finding's framing: the work runs inside `spawn_blocking`, so runtime worker threads are not blocked (only the shared `gate` serializes), and `machines.rebuild` (machines/registry.rs:66-70) early-returns when `config.hosts` is unchanged, so the preamble cost is the config read/parse/merge plus a spawn_blocking hop, not a registry rebuild. That makes 'high' severity overstated — on a local disk this is tens of microseconds per keystroke — but the defect (uncached, globally serialized disk IO on the PTY input path) is real.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/stores/config.rs and its inline tests; potentially crates/fleet-daemon/src/adapters/files.rs (Files trait + RealFiles + every fake/test-support impl) if a freshness probe beyond the existing `metadata()` is needed. Tests that write config.json out of band and expect the next `load()` to observe it must keep passing: server/connection.rs:733 and :1081, services/sleep.rs:576, services/snapshots.rs:311/:381, services/maintenance.rs:680, services/sessions/tests.rs:19, services/worktrees.rs:715/:899.
corrected_fix: Cache, but do not invalidate only on `save`/`update` — the daemon has no config watcher and the product deliberately supports hand edits (docs/KEYMAP.md:377 and docs/UX-SPEC.md:1299: `E` opens config.json in a terminal tab), so a save-invalidated cache would silently stop honouring external edits. Validate the cached `Arc<Config>` with a cheap stat each load: `Files::metadata` (adapters/files.rs:78) already returns a device+inode `FileIdentity`, and `atomic_write_text` is temp+rename (files.rs:356), so every well-behaved write changes the inode; add len+mtime to `FileMetadata` if in-place appends must also be caught. Return `Arc<Config>` and keep the `gate` only around the reload. Reject the second alternative in the proposal (skipping the preamble for terminal requests): `router.route` consults `self.machines` (services/router/mod.rs:114-126) which is populated by the preamble's `machines.rebuild(&config)`, and terminal requests are routable to remote hosts, so skipping it changes routing behaviour.

rule: rust-gpui-testing checklist, Fakes and seams: "Does a new external dependency (process, socket, filesystem, clock…) arrive behind a trait in adapters/? nothing calls Command::new, Utc::now or std::fs directly" + Determinism: "Is a timeout proven by stepping past its constant?"
summary: The hot-pool staleness decision reads `Utc::now()` directly instead of the injectable `Clock` adapter, and no test in the workspace ever exercises the `age >= config.hot_freshness_ms` branch — the default 60 s window makes it unreachable in a test.
evidence:
crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/pool.rs:437 `fetched_at: Utc::now().to_rfc3339(),` and :481-485
```rust
let age = Utc::now().signed_duration_since(fetched).num_milliseconds();
if age < 0
    || u64::try_from(age).unwrap_or(u64::MAX) >= config.hot_freshness_ms
```
`Pool::new` (`:51-58`) takes `config, state, jobs, git, files, shell` — no `Arc<dyn Clock>`, even though `crates/fleet-daemon/src/adapters/clock.rs:6-14` defines the port and `testing::fakes::FixedClock` implements it. `grep -rn "hotFreshnessMs\|hot_freshness"` across `crates/` returns no test: only `config.rs:280,331,642` and two settings-dialog call sites.
failure_scenario: Invert the comparison to `<=` or drop the `age` clause entirely and every test still passes: `pool_build_claim_refill_and_snapshot_status` and `force_runs_forced_successor` (crates/fleet-daemon/tests/pool_lifecycle.rs:83,164) both run inside the 60 s window, so a slot is always "fresh" there and the aging branch is never taken. In production that means a stale prepared worktree — wrong `origin/main`, hours old — is handed to `claim` and the user starts work on a stale base with no fetch.
proposed_fix: Add `clock: Arc<dyn Clock>` to `Pool::new`, use `self.clock.now()` in `write_hot_marker` and `slot_is_fresh`, and thread `SystemClock` from the composition root. Then a test can pin the clock and step past `hot_freshness_ms`.
test_plan: `a_prepared_slot_past_its_freshness_window_is_rebuilt_before_it_is_claimed`: build a `Pool` on `FakeFiles` + `FixedClock`, `prepare`, capture the marker's `sha`, advance the `FixedClock` past `config.hot_freshness_ms`, point `FakeShell`'s `git rev-parse origin/main` rule at a new sha, `prepare` again and assert the marker was rewritten (and `claim` hands back the rebuilt slot). Removing the `age >= config.hot_freshness_ms` clause makes it fail; today nothing does.
verify_reason: Coverage gap verified. `slot_is_fresh` (services/pool.rs:467-495) gates the refresh decision in `prepare_job` (:227-249). `grep hot_freshness` across crates/ hits only fleet-core/src/config.rs:280,331 and pool.rs:484 plus two settings-dialog sites — no test. tests/pool_lifecycle.rs:83 and :164 both prepare twice within the same second (60 s default window) and tests/pool_fake_claim.rs exercises `claim_into_locked` (:108-128), which never consults freshness at all. Dropping the `age >=` clause leaves the sha comparison, and the sha is re-read from the slot's own `origin/<branch>` ref, which cannot change without a fetch — so the mutation self-confirms freshness forever and nothing fails.
blast_radius: Test-only under the corrected fix: crates/fleet-daemon/tests/pool_lifecycle.rs (or a new tests/pool_freshness.rs). Under the finding's original fix instead: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/pool.rs, services/composition.rs:89, services/worktrees.rs:101 and :456, tests/pool_lifecycle.rs:113,194 and tests/pool_fake_claim.rs:41 all change signature.
corrected_fix: REJECT the proposed Clock injection into `Pool::new` — it is unnecessary for this test and touches four construction sites. `hot_freshness_ms` is plain config (`"hotFreshnessMs"`, camelCase per fleet-core/src/config.rs:20/280), so a test can `config.update(json!({"hotFreshnessMs": 0}))` after the first `prepare`, then `prepare` again and assert the `.hot/.git/swarm-hot.json` marker was rewritten (compare `fetched_at`) and that a fetch ran; pair it with the existing 60 s-window case that asserts the marker is untouched. Those two together kill both the 'drop the age clause' and 'invert the comparison' mutations, with no production change. Only introduce `Arc<dyn Clock>` into `Pool` if you separately want the adapter-purity rule enforced for pool.rs:437's `Utc::now()` — that is a different change, and if made, `write_hot_marker` and `slot_is_fresh` must use the same clock or the staleness maths goes inconsistent.

rule: rust-gpui-testing checklist, Fakes and seams: "Does the fake implement the *same* trait production uses — no parallel API? A fake that drifts from the real impl is worse than no fake."
summary: `FakeShell::run_streaming` returns the rule's `stdout`/`stderr` inside the `ShellResult` and ignores `command.timeout`, while `RealShell::run_streaming` always returns empty `stdout`/`stderr` and can return `DaemonError::Timeout`; service tests therefore assert output that production never produces.
failure_scenario: `services/update.rs:94-96` does `let result = context.spawn_child(shell, cargo …).await?; result.require_success("cargo build --release")?;` and `require_success` (adapters/shell.rs:107-116) formats the message with `concise_output(&self.stderr, &self.stdout)`. Under `FakeShell` the test at `services/update.rs:186-196` feeds 1000 lines of stderr, so the fake produces `"cargo build --release exited 7: build diagnostic…"`; under `RealShell` stderr and stdout are always empty, so the real daemon reports `"cargo build --release exited 7: "` with no diagnostic at all. The test is named `update_reports_verbose_build_success_and_failure` and cannot detect that. Symmetrically, no service test can ever reach the `StreamingCompletion::TimedOut` arm, because the fake never honours `command.timeout`.
proposed_fix: Make the fake match the contract: return `ShellResult { status, stdout: String::new(), stderr: String::new() }` from `run_streaming` after emitting the lines through `on_line`, and add a `timeout` rule so a rule can request `Err(DaemonError::Timeout(..))` when `command.timeout` is set. Then fix `Update` to build its failure message from the streamed lines it recorded, not from `result.stderr`.
test_plan: Add a shared-contract test next to `fake_and_real_files_preserve_directory_trees` (crates/fleet-daemon/src/testing/files.rs:479): `fake_and_real_shells_agree_on_streaming_results` runs `sh -c 'echo out; echo err 1>&2; exit 3'` through `RealShell` and the equivalent rule through `FakeShell`, and asserts both return `status == 3` with empty `stdout`/`stderr` and both delivered `["out", "err"]` through `on_line`. It fails today on the `FakeShell` half. Add `a_failed_streaming_build_still_names_its_diagnostics` in `services/update.rs` asserting the job's failure text contains a streamed line — it fails until `Update` stops reading `result.stderr`.
verify_reason: Drift is real: crates/fleet-daemon/src/testing/fakes.rs:115-130 returns `self.matching(&command)` verbatim (stdout+stderr populated) and ignores `command.timeout`, while crates/fleet-daemon/src/adapters/shell.rs:283-288 always returns empty `stdout`/`stderr` on the `Exited` arm and :299-303 returns `DaemonError::Timeout` on `TimedOut`. Same trait, divergent contract. Two corrections to the finding, though: (a) the cited test at services/update.rs:161-193 asserts only `error.contains("cargo build --release")`, i.e. the operation prefix — it does not assert the streamed diagnostic, so the finding's 'the test asserts output production never produces' is overstated; (b) the diagnostics are not lost in production — jobs/job.rs:91-108 pipes every streamed line into `context.progress`, so the build output lands in the job log; only the one-line failure summary from `require_success` (adapters/shell.rs:107-116 -> concise_output :407-414) degrades to `"cargo build --release exited 7: "`. Severity is medium, not high.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/testing/fakes.rs; the only production `run_streaming` caller is crates/fleet-daemon/src/jobs/job.rs:91 via crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/update.rs:89, so test fallout is confined to update.rs `mod tests` (`update_reports_verbose_build_success_and_failure`, `cancelled_update_never_starts_build_commands`) — neither reads the streamed stdout/stderr today. crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/hosts.rs:630 panics in `run_streaming` and is unaffected.
corrected_fix: Two separable changes. (1) Make the fake honour the contract: `run_streaming` emits the rule's lines through `on_line`, then returns `ShellResult { status: result.status, stdout: String::new(), stderr: String::new() }`; add a rule flag so a rule can yield `Err(DaemonError::Timeout(subcommand(&command)))` when `command.timeout` is set, so the `TimedOut` arm becomes reachable in service tests. (2) Do NOT 'fix Update to build its message from result.stderr' — instead have `JobCtx::spawn_child` retain a bounded tail (say the last 20 lines) of the streamed output and expose it, so `Update` can attach it to the failure; blindly buffering all output would reintroduce the unbounded-memory reason RealShell returns empty strings (the update rule streams 1000+ lines). If that is more than the cleanup warrants, the minimum correct change is (1) plus asserting in update's test that the failure names the operation only.

rule: rust-gpui-testing checklist, Determinism/Coverage: a test that reports success without running its body is "a deleted test with extra steps"; "Is platform gating #[cfg] rather than a runtime early return? A runtime skip reports as a pass."
summary: `isolated_test` re-executes the test binary with `--exact <name>` and only checks the child's exit status; libtest exits 0 when the filter matches nothing, so any drift between the hand-written name literal and the function name silently turns ten tests into no-ops that still report as passing.
failure_scenario: Rename `immediate_exit_is_registered` (`:676`) to `an_immediate_exit_is_registered` and leave the literal at `:677` alone. The parent invocation now spawns the child with `--exact immediate_exit_is_registered`; libtest matches zero tests, prints `0 passed; 0 failed; 10 filtered out`, and exits 0. The parent's `assert!(output.status.success())` holds, `isolated_test` returns `true`, the parent returns early, and the whole PTY/session lifecycle assertion set never executes — while `cargo test` reports the test as passing. The same happens if `FLEET_SESSION_TEST` is set in the developer's environment for a different name.
proposed_fix: Derive the name instead of retyping it (`fn isolated_test(name: &str)` called with a `stringify!`-based macro, or `concat!` on the fn name), and assert the child actually ran one test: parse the child's stdout for `1 passed` (or pass `--format terse` and require exactly one `.` line) before returning `true`.
test_plan: Add `the_isolation_harness_fails_when_the_child_runs_no_test`: call the (extracted) child-runner with a name that matches nothing, e.g. `run_isolated_child("no_such_session_test")`, and assert it panics/returns `Err`. It fails today — the helper returns success — and passes once the helper requires `1 passed` in the child's output.
verify_reason: Mechanism proven empirically, not just argued: I built a one-test libtest binary and ran `./t --exact no_such_test` — 'running 0 tests ... test result: ok. 0 passed; 1 filtered out', exit=0. crates/fleet-daemon/tests/sessions_lifecycle.rs:775-799 asserts only `output.status.success()`, so a name-literal/function-name divergence silently converts a test into a no-op that reports as a pass. Two corrections: (a) all ten literals currently match their function names (checked every call site at :117,180,266,306,342,493,604,677,722 against the fn on the preceding line), so nothing is inert today — this is latent hardening, not a live defect; (b) the 'FLEET_SESSION_TEST set for a different name' half of the failure scenario is wrong — `.env_clear()` at :784 means the child's environment is built from scratch, and a stray parent-side value for another test's name only makes that other test run its body in the un-isolated parent, which fails loudly rather than passing silently.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/tests/sessions_lifecycle.rs only — the helper is file-local and its ten call sites keep their signature.
corrected_fix: Skip the `stringify!`/`concat!` half of the proposal — Rust has no stable way to name the enclosing function, so a macro wrapper would still be hand-maintained. Just make the child prove it ran: capture stdout and, after the success assert, `assert!(stdout.contains("1 passed"), "isolated child ran no test: {name}")` (or spawn with `--format terse` and require exactly one `.`). That single added assertion turns every future rename into a hard failure.
